_comment: Real-landscape validation manifest.
SKELETON written by tests/scripts/harvest_octopus.py -- hand-edit the
'description' and any narrative caveats; the numeric fields (bbox,
target_epsg, octopus_source, run_params) are complete as written.
The DEM is fetched KEYLESS (Copernicus GLO-30) into a temp workdir by
run_cosmo_validation.py, compared, then deleted. No large data is
ever committed.
description: DiBiase et al. (2010) San Gabriel Mountains 10Be basins, California (OCTOPUS S055). A compact West-Fork cluster of 15 small catchments (0.08-6.4 km2), 1533-2079 m, STEEP and high-relief (OCTOPUS SLP_AVE ~363, ELEV_STD ~203 m) with basin-averaged erosion rates 37-583 mm/kyr -- an order of magnitude faster than the pilot Front Range (dethier2014, 14-56 mm/kyr) and the arid Clapp basins (clapp2002, 18-30 mm/kyr). A deliberately STEEP / HIGH-RELIEF contrast that also carries the largest topographic-shielding departures (BETOPO down to 0.98 in this cluster, more study-wide), feeding the parallel topo-shielding / numerics investigation. One sample with >100% analytical uncertainty (S055WTS004) was dropped by the harvester's max_rel_uncertainty filter.

published_reference.citation: DiBiase, R.A., Whipple, K.X., Heimsath, A.M., Ouimet, W.B. (2010), Earth Planet. Sci. Lett. 289(1-2), 134-144.
published_reference.calculator: OCTOPUS v2.3(4) recalculation with CAIRN (Mudd et al. 2016), default Stone/Lal 'St' scaling (EBE_* fields).

_comment: Regression targets harvested from OCTOPUS, NOT scraped or invented.
OCTOPUS recalculates with CAIRN = the algorithm lsdtt-cosmo-tool
implements, so a NEAR-CAIRN oracle (see residual_expectation).
octopus_source.cql_note: Filter with CQL_FILTER, not bbox: the OCTOPUS WFS 2.0.0 bbox parameter throws a ProjectionException.
octopus_source.scaling_scheme: St (Stone/Lal) -- EBE_MMKYR / EBE_GCMYR. OCTOPUS also stores EBEL/EBELNS (LSDn).

_comment: UPDATED 2026-07-24 (standardisation double-count FIXED; see pilot
dethier2014_manifest standardisation_convention + §6e). This dataset already
read ~-5% before the fix (its samples are mostly 07KNSTD, so the double-count
barely touched it); it stays ~-5.25% after. The clapp2002 dataset moved from
+6.6% to -4%, so the earlier 'sign flip' between the two was an ARTEFACT of the
standardisation bug -- all three datasets now share one uniform -4..-6% muon
offset (lsdtt3 LOWER).
residual_expectation.band: frozen 2026-07-24 (post-fix): 14 reliable basins -11.45 to +3.08% (mean -5.25%); WTS044 flagged delineation-unreliable. Steep high-relief, so larger per-basin scatter (ignored per-pixel topo shielding + delineation on small steep catchments).
residual_expectation.attribute_residual_to: muon scheme (BraucherBorchers vs Braucher, intentional) as the systematic offset; per-basin scatter from ignored per-pixel topo shielding (steepest terrain) + delineation -- NOT standardisation (fixed), NOT a bug. Matched to OCTOPUS lsdtt3 reproduces CAIRN to ~0% (see pilot decisive_result).

dem.dem_source_note: Keyless. lsdtt-fetch-raster retrieves+clips Copernicus GLO-30 from AWS Open Data (cop30_aws) or Microsoft Planetary Computer (planetary_computer) with NO API key.
dem.target_epsg_note: UTM zone from OCTOPUS PROJEPSGID=32611. The cosmo CLIs require a PROJECTED CRS, so the DEM is warped to UTM at fetch time.
dem.resolution_choice_note: COP30 (30 m) vs the DEM in the OCTOPUS/CAIRN recalculation is a DOCUMENTED, attributable validation difference, not a bug.

bounding_box._comment: Union of the 15 selected basins' OCTOPUS polygon bounds, padded 0.02 deg.

_comment: lsdtt-cosmo-tool run knobs. threshold_contributing_pixels lowered
from the 1000 default (= 0.9 km2 at 30 m) so sub-km2 basins
delineate near their true size; basins below this*cellsize^2 remain
unreliable (outlet snaps onto a larger channel) and are flagged in
the summary. To match OCTOPUS's atmosphere add 'atmosphere: NCEP'
(default ERA40).
